papers.abstract: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab improves survival in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. We evaluated this combination as neoadjuvant therapy and investigated its effect on peripheral immunity and the tumour microenvironment. PRIME-HCC is a single-arm, phase 1b trial in adults (aged ≥18 years) with early-stage resectable hepatocellular carcinoma, Child-Pugh A liver function, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-1. Patients received nivolumab (3 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 22 of the first and second cycle) and ipilimumab (1 mg/kg intravenously on day 1 of the first cycle only) before liver resection. The primary endpoint was safety, assessed by treatment-related delays to surgery and adverse events in the intention-to-treat population. Translational analyses included imaging mass cytometry and spatial transcriptomics on paired tumour samples, peripheral immunophenotyping, T-cell receptor (TCR) β sequencing, and longitudinal tumour-agnostic circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) profiling. This trial was registered with EudraCT (2018-000987-27) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03682276); follow-up is currently ongoing. Between Sept 18, 2019, and Sept 28, 2023, of 43 patients assessed for eligibility, 33 patients were enrolled (25 [76%] male and 8 [24%] female; median age 68 years [range 38-80; IQR 63-73]); median follow-up was 25·7 months (95% CI 21·2-30·1). Any-grade adverse events occurred in 31 (94%) of patients, with treatment-related adverse events (trAEs) in 25 (76%) patients. Grade 3 trAEs occurred in three (9%) patients (transaminase elevation, anaemia, and dyspnoea). Serious adverse events were recorded in three (9%) patients, and no grade 4-5 events or treatment-related deaths occurred. 30 (91%) patients underwent surgery, including two (6%) who had immune checkpoint inhibitor-related surgical delays. Objective response rate by RECIST 1.1 was noted in eight (25%; 95% CI 13-42) patients (one complete response and seven partial responses), with 31 (97%; 84-100) patients achieving disease control. The absence of ctDNA after surgery was associated with improved 2-year recurrence-free survival (nine [82%] of 11 patients vs two [29%] of seven; p=0·049), as was at least 50% ctDNA reduction (median not reached [95% CI not reached] vs 20·9 months [95% CI 16·3-25·4]; HR 0·14 [95% CI 0·02-0·91]; p=0·039). Patients with objective responses showed expansion of peripheral PD-1-positive, Ki-67-positive, CD8-positive T cells (T-responding exhausted cells [Tresp]), associated with higher baseline intratumoral progenitor-exhausted T cells (Tpex) and increased Tresp infiltration. Patients whose disease did not respond to treatment exhibited enrichment of terminally exhausted CD8-positive T cells (Tex-term; CD8-positive PD-1-positive TOX-positive cells) and regulatory T cells. Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab is feasible in early-stage resectable hepatocellular carcinoma, and later-phase randomised trials are needed to confirm the efficacy of this treatment strategy. Longitudinal ctDNA monitoring could support detection of minimal residual disease and warrants further prospective validation. papers.abstract: Patient experience is a core dimension of oncology care quality, but cognitive burden, emotional distress, and complex care trajectories in brain metastases populations may limit traditional survey approaches. This study evaluated the feasibility and interpretability of a locally developed, self-administered patient experience survey administered after initial brain-directed intervention within a multidisciplinary brain metastases program. We conducted a prospective quality improvement evaluation of a patient experience survey administered on tablets at follow-up visits two to three months after initial consultation. Eligible participants were new patients seen in a multidisciplinary brain metastases clinic. Descriptive statistics characterized response patterns, including agreement rates, "not applicable" responses, and missing data. Reasons for non-completion were categorized descriptively. Among 70 eligible patients, 41 completed the survey (59%). Overall ratings were high, with most respondents reporting that they were always treated with courtesy and respect and always received the best care possible. Communication and decision-making items showed high agreement. Treatment-dependent items showed reduced applicability, including explanations of medication and treatment impact on daily activities, with substantial "not applicable" responses. A subset strongly disagreed with items addressing clarity of results and functional impact. Open-ended responses were generally positive despite structured disagreement. Surveys administered after brain-directed intervention yielded high overall experience ratings but revealed variation in domain applicability, which may reflect treatment exposure and position along the disease trajectory. As a single cross-sectional administration of an instrument without formal psychometric validation, these findings primarily inform survey feasibility and design; trajectory-informed assessment strategies warrant prospective evaluation.

papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has transformed the treatment of B-cell malignancies, but insufficient expansion and persistence, progressive T-cell dysfunction, and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments continue to limit durable efficacy and broader application. Cytokines are central regulators of both T-cell fitness and interactions with surrounding immune cells, providing a rationale for incorporating cytokine signals directly into engineered cellular therapies. Here we trace the development and clinical translation of cytokine-enhanced CAR T cells from the pioneering studies with IL-12 to common g-chain cytokines and IL-18. IL-12 established the potential of engineered T cells to deliver potent inflammatory signals locally and mobilize endogenous immunity, but also revealed the risk of systemic inflammatory toxicity. Common g-chain cytokines, particularly IL-7, IL-15 and IL-21, have predominantly been exploited to promote expansion, persistence and favorable differentiation states, with several approaches advancing to clinical testing. IL-18 combines direct support of engineered T cells with recruitment and remodeling of endogenous immune compartments and has recently demonstrated encouraging clinical activity in hematologic malignancies. Emerging strategies increasingly extend beyond cytokine secretion to inducible circuits, synthetic cytokine receptors, unconventional cytokines and combinations of complementary signals. Rational selection of cytokines for specific disease contexts, together with precise spatial and temporal control of their activity, will be critical to balance efficacy against toxicity and realize the full potential of cytokine-engineered cellular therapies.

papers.abstract: To compare image quality and radiation-dose indices between photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) and conventional energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) examinations in patients with multiple myeloma. This retrospective intraindividual study included 47 patients with non-contrast whole-body PCCT examinations (NAEOTOM Alpha, Siemens Healthineers) and prior EID-CT examinations (SOMATOM Sensation 64, Siemens Healthineers). Examinations were performed using the respective clinical protocols, which differed in acquisition and reconstruction settings. Quantitative image analysis included region-of-interest measurements in the lungs, spleen, muscle, and adipose tissue. Image noise and signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) were calculated. For qualitative assessment, two radiologists independently evaluated randomized and anonymized PCCT and EID-CT scans of the same patients using a 5-point Likert scale to rate overall image quality, sharpness, noise, and osteolytic lesion conspicuity. Qualitative ratings were compared separately for each reader using two-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Differences in CT-dose-index, dose-length-product, and quantitative image metrics were analyzed using two-sided paired t-tests. Quantitative analysis demonstrated significantly lower image noise in PCCT compared to EID-CT in the spleen, muscle, and adipose tissue (p < 0.0001), but not in lung tissue (p = 0.27). SNR was significantly higher with PCCT in all tissues except the lungs (p < 0.0001; lungs: p = 0.22; adipose tissue: p = 0.02). Qualitative assessment showed that PCCT was rated significantly better than EID-CT for overall image quality, image sharpness, noise, and osteolysis conspicuity (p < 0.0001 for all categories). Radiation dose parameters (CTDIvol and DLP) were significantly lower with PCCT than with EID-CT (p < 0.0001). In non-contrast whole-body imaging of patients with multiple myeloma, the evaluated PCCT system provided superior image quality and significantly lower radiation-dose indices than the historical EID-CT system. These findings reflect the combined performance of the imaging systems and their respective acquisition and reconstruction settings.

papers.abstract: Accessing tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells in patient blood is essential for non-invasive monitoring of systemic T cell responses and guiding personalized therapies. However, precise functional, molecular, and phenotypic characterization of these cells remains challenging. Here, we identify TIGIT as a functionally validated surrogate marker of tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells and define its associated transcriptional program to characterize circulating tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells in melanoma patients. We demonstrate that blood TIGIT⁺ CD8⁺ T cells mount robust cytotoxic responses against autologous tumor cells across multiple melanoma patient models, irrespective of PD-1 co-expression. At the clonotype level, TIGIT broadened detection of the circulating tumor-reactive repertoire beyond PD-1 while retaining high specificity. Moreover, circulating TIGIT⁺ CD8⁺ T cell population was closely associated with the intratumoral T cell repertoire and exhibited hallmarks of antigen experience, including effector memory differentiation, a hypomethylated DNA landscape, and increased clonal expansion. Longitudinal profiling of blood samples from melanoma patients undergoing immune checkpoint inhibition revealed an increased frequency of TIGIT⁺ CD8⁺ T cells in clinical responders. Finally, leveraging paired single-cell transcriptomic and TCR data from patient models with identified tumor-reactive clones, we show that the TIGIT-associated transcriptional program enables robust detection of circulating tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells. Collectively, our data establish TIGIT⁺ CD8⁺ T cells as a potent reservoir of tumor-reactive T cells in peripheral blood and provide a blood-based framework for accelerating TCR discovery and advancing adoptive cell therapy.

papers.abstract: To improve ICI efficacy in advanced CC, a promising strategy is to combine anti-PDL-1, anti-CTLA-4 and chemotherapy. The phase I/II MOVIE trial reported a clinical benefit rate of 53.1% of durvalumab, tremelimumab and metronomic oral vinorelbine in patients with pretreated metastatic CC. The objective of this study is to discover immune efficacy biomarkers of this combination. We analyzed 29 advanced CC patients from MOVIE multicentric prospective clinical trial (NCT03518606). We used high-dimensional mass cytometry (CyTOF) to explore the immune landscape in baseline peripheral blood mononuclear cells. We developed 3 immune panels of 40 antibodies (T cells, NK cells and myeloid cells) for the deep-phenotyping of PBMCs. Our bioinformatics workflow of CyTOF data included dimensionality reduction (opt-SNE, UMAP), automated clustering (PhenoGraph) and regression (CITRUS). The biomarker candidates were submitted to a model prediction composed of 11 machine-learning algorithms. In baseline blood samples, high-dimensional analyses consistently identified a population of TOX+TIGIT+CD57+ TEMRA (CD45RA+CCR7-) CD8+ T cells associated with improved clinical outcomes: clinical benefit (CB), progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). This population was confirmed by manual gating and 11 machine-learning algorithms. After determining a cut-off at 0.73% of CD45+ cells, patients with an increased blood baseline frequency of TOX+TIGIT+CD57+ TEMRA (CD45RA+CCR7-) CD8+ T cells had an improved CBR (76% vs 25%, p=0.005), an improved PFS (HR=0.35, CI95, 0.13-0.95, p=0.013) and an improved OS (HR=0.19, CI95, 0.07-0.53, p=0.001). Multivariate analysis with classical CC prognostic factors confirmed the OS benefit of our biomarker (HR=0.15, CI95: 0.05-0.47, <0.001).

papers.abstract: Controversy remains regarding the effect of inspired oxygen fraction (FIO2) on postoperative lung aeration. We sought to evaluate whether lowering FIO2 solely during emergence from anesthesia reduces immediate postoperative loss of lung aeration, assessed by lung ultrasonography. In this double-blind multicentre randomized controlled trial, we allocated 102 patients undergoing laparoscopic gastrectomy to either a low- or high-FIO2 group (FIO2 = 0.5 vs 0.8 during emergence, respectively). The primary outcome was the lung ultrasonography score (LUS) measured in the postanesthesia care unit (PACU). Secondary outcomes were the Oxygen Reserve Index™ (ORi™) after extubation, atelectasis on chest radiography taken on postoperative day (POD) 2, and oxygen desaturation events in the PACU and within the first 48 postoperative hr. The median [interquartile range (IQR)] LUS did not significantly differ between the two groups (low-FIO2 group, 3 [2-5] vs high-FIO2 group, 3 [2-6]; P = 0.48). The median [IQR] ORi values after extubation were 0.42 [0.10-0.74] and 0.52 [0.30-0.83] in the low- and high-FIO2 groups, respectively (adjusted P = 0.36). The incidence of atelectasis on chest radiography on POD 2 (low-FIO2 group, 57% vs high-FIO2 group, 49%; P = 0.43; adjusted P > 0.99) and other pulmonary complication rates were not different between the groups. Lowering the FIO2 from 0.8 to 0.5 during the anesthesia emergence period alone did not reduce immediate postoperative LUS after laparoscopic gastrectomy. Routine reduction of the FIO2 < 0.8 during emergence solely for the purpose of preserving postoperative lung aeration may have limited clinical value in a relatively low-risk patient population. papers.abstract: Cutaneous melanoma exhibits strong responses to immunotherapy, yet the system-level mechanisms linking mutational burden, genomic alterations, antigen landscapes, post-transcriptional and post-translational regulation, and immune outcomes remain incompletely defined. We profiled 183 cutaneous melanomas using 13 omic layers, including immunopeptidomics, metabolomics, protein ubiquitylation and glycosylation, to construct a holistic view of tumor immunogenicity. Mass spectrometry-based HLA-I immunopeptidomics revealed correlation between tumor antigens and CD8+ T-cell infiltration. Metabolomics revealed distinct ether-linked lipids and mitochondrial metabolic profiles between primary and metastatic tumors. Ubiquitylomics uncovered a subset of tumors associated with worse survival, characterized by high ubiquitylation of the IFN signaling pathway and ubiquitylation-dependent activation of AKT1. Glycoproteomic analyses identified GPNMB glycosylation as a key feature associated with sex-specific survival, linking this signal to a lysosome-associated program and suggesting potential sex-dependent differences in immunotherapy response. This multi-omic atlas of cutaneous melanoma illuminates mechanisms of immune evasion, informing treatment-relevant patient stratification in melanoma care.

papers.abstract: Obesity is one of the most difficult challenges of the modern era, affecting more than 1 billion people worldwide. Nearly half of US adults and 1 in 5 US children meet the medical definition of having obesity, with major consequences for cardiometabolic, kidney, hepatic, pulmonary, musculoskeletal, reproductive, oncologic, and mental health. Obesity also carries social and economic harms through stigma, discrimination, and bias. Drivers of the obesity epidemic include changes in food production and consumption accompanied by social, economic, and technological shifts that reduce food preparation, disrupt sleep, and decrease physical activity. The burden of these changes is not equally distributed, with higher obesity prevalence among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. Current prevention measures include nutrition standards, food and menu labeling, school meal policies, sugar-sweetened beverage taxes, community-based lifestyle programs, and public assistance efforts. The impact of these approaches has been inadequate. Contemporary clinical management recognizes obesity as a chronic disease characterized by genetic, biological, and behavioral susceptibilities. Access, affordability, tolerability, and the chronicity of use remain major challenges for all available obesity management strategies, including new glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapies. Potential solutions require a coordinated, multisector response and include efforts to prevent obesity at the societal level, improve care of individuals with obesity, and strengthen research and innovation. Priority areas include improving the food and physical activity environment; strengthening communication and education; strengthening childhood obesity prevention; addressing health inequities; reducing stigma and bias; modernizing obesity care delivery; expanding access to lifestyle, healthy food, medication, and surgical interventions; and supporting long-term treatment adherence and maintenance. Proposed actions include new government policies on food production, labeling, marketing, and school nutrition; modernization of drug evaluation; payment reform to support comprehensive obesity treatment; development of multidisciplinary care models; incentives to promote cross-sector partnerships; and research to advance personalized prevention and treatment strategies. The emergence of effective obesity management medications offers a significant opportunity to curb the prevalence of obesity. However, no single intervention will be enough. Sustained improvement will require addressing the underlying structural and environmental drivers of obesity, along with person-centered, multilevel strategies that simultaneously improve prevention, reduce stigma, and expand equitable access to evidence-based treatment. Coordinated action across government, health care systems, clinicians, payers, industry, schools, communities, and researchers will be essential to achieving long-term improvement.

papers.abstract: Intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) allows real-time assessment of the anesthetic state of the brain and offers a means of titrating anesthetic delivery in children. Randomized trials have shown that EEG-guided titration reduces anesthetic exposure, shortens emergence and recovery, and lowers the incidence of emergence delirium, yet routine use outside research settings has remained largely confined to enthusiastic clinicians and clinical trials. To describe the adoption of routine intraoperative raw EEG monitoring over time at a quaternary pediatric hospital, to characterize practice variation among anesthesia providers, and to identify patient and procedural factors associated with EEG use. We conducted a retrospective single-center study of anesthetic records in the electronic health record from 17 October 2024, when automated EEG capture began, to 30 June 2026, following departmental implementation of routine raw EEG monitoring. Providers were categorized by EEG use as high (> 40% of cases), moderate (20%-40%) or low (< 20%). Trend, provider-level, and procedural associations with EEG use were examined using segmented regression, mixed-effects logistic regression, and clustered logistic regression. Of 26 168 analyzed cases, 21.7% (5674) involved intraoperative EEG monitoring, provided by 59 staff anesthesiologists, 9 senior fellows, 24 fellows, and 102 residents. EEG use rose from 17.8% of cases in October 2024 to 28.4% in June 2026. Use varied widely among staff anesthesiologists (median 18.1%, IQR 12.3%-31.3%; range 0.9%-79.5%); 59.3% (35/59) were low users, and 18.6% (11/59) were high users, with the five highest users accounting for 27.0% of all EEG-monitored cases managed by staff. Case mix explained only a small proportion of this variation (pseudo R2 = 0.064). EEG-monitored cases were more often longer, involved neuromuscular blockade, TIVA maintenance, cardiac surgery, and trainee presence. Adoption of routine raw EEG monitoring increased steadily but nonlinearly following implementation. Variation in use among providers was only weakly explained by case mix, indicating that individual practice patterns, more than patient or procedural characteristics, drove uptake. Efforts to broaden EEG monitoring may benefit from targeting low-use providers and during fellowship training.

papers.abstract: The phase 3 ATTLAS study demonstrated that atezolizumab plus bevacizumab, carboplatin, and paclitaxel (ABCP) improved progression-free survival compared with pemetrexed-carboplatin/cisplatin (PC) in EGFR/ALK-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer after tyrosine kinase inhibitor failure. We report patient-reported quality of life (QoL) outcomes. Patients received ABCP (atezolizumab 1200 mg, bevacizumab 15 mg/kg, carboplatin AUC 5-5.5, paclitaxel 175 mg/m2) or PC (pemetrexed 500 mg/m2, carboplatin AUC 5.0, or cisplatin 70 mg/m2) every 3 weeks. QoL was assessed using EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-LC13. Primary endpoints were changes in global health status/QoL (GHS/QoL) from baseline at weeks 9 and 24, and median time to deterioration (TTD; ≥ 10-point decline). Of 228 randomized patients (2:1), 146 (ABCP) and 68 (PC) completed ≥ 1 QoL assessment. Baseline GHS/QoL was comparable between arms. Early GHS and physical functioning scores were numerically lower with ABCP but stabilized by week 24, with no significant differences at week 9 (-4.66; p = 0.247) or week 24 (-7.39; p = 0.305). Toxicity-related symptoms (neuropathy, alopecia, and pain) were more frequent with ABCP, whereas cancer-related symptom improvements (cough, dyspnea, and hemoptysis) occurred in both arms without significant differences. Median TTD was 3.48 months (ABCP) versus 6.90 months (PC; p = 0.160). Despite impairment in symptoms commonly associated with chemotherapy, no significant between-group difference in overall QoL was detected between ABCP and PC. Stable GHS/QoL and improvement in cancer-related symptoms were observed alongside appropriate toxicity management. The protocol was approved by the institutional review board of Samsung Medical Center (IRB no. 2019-03-027) and participating centers (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03991403).

papers.abstract: Chronic diseases are still treated largely with interventions that are constitutive, intermittently administered and poorly aligned with real-time physiology. Synthetic biology is changing this paradigm by treating gene circuits as programmable genetic software that can be deployed across cellular therapeutic hardware spanning from prokaryotic to eukaryotic systems, including probiotic cells, designer cells, immune cells and stem‑cell‑derived platforms. In this framework, engineered systems can sense disease-associated signals, compute them through synthetic or repurposed transduction pathways and adjust therapeutic output to maintain physiological variables within a desired range. Closed-loop therapeutics therefore begin to merge diagnosis, treatment and prevention within the same living platform. Across metabolism, inflammation, infection, cardiovascular regulation and cancer, early mammalian systems show that endogenous sensing, intracellular computation and therapeutic actuation can be combined in clinically relevant architectures. The emerging concept of setpoint medicine captures the clinical ambition of these systems: not simply to deliver a dose, but to keep physiology within an interpretable and therapeutically desirable range. Realizing this vision will require durable and modular control circuits, hardware-aware delivery strategies, interpretable safety frameworks, controller-style performance metrics and increasingly AI-assisted design, calibration and oversight. If these challenges can be met, the future of therapy may be defined less by intermittent dosing than by the continuous control of physiology.

papers.abstract: Early surgical intervention, including debridement and grafting, is crucial in acute burn injury management. Although early extubation in operating rooms (ORs) reduces intensive care unit length of stay and ventilator-associated complications, extubation feasibility following initial burn surgery remains uncertain. We investigated perioperative factors associated with postoperative continuation of mechanical ventilation (MV) after initial burn surgery. This retrospective study analyzed patients with burns who underwent acute-phase debridement between 2018 and 2024. Patients requiring postoperative MV were compared with those extubated in ORs. Factors independently associated with postoperative MV were identified using multivariate logistic regression analysis. Among 418 patients, 75 required postoperative MV. Age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.03, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.00-1.06), percentage of total body surface area (%TBSA) burned (aOR = 1.08, 95% CI 1.03-1.12), preoperative intubation (aOR = 11.8, 95% CI 3.02-46.4), intraoperative fluid administration volume (ml/kg) (aOR = 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.06), and intraoperative maximum vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) (aOR = 1.18, 95% CI 1.10-1.26) were independently associated with postoperative MV continuation. This association between the intraoperative maximum VIS and postoperative MV continuation was maintained in the sensitivity analysis excluding preoperatively intubated patients (aOR = 1.16, 95% CI 1.08-1.25). Age, %TBSA burned, preoperative intubation, intraoperative fluid administration volume, and maximum intraoperative VIS were independently associated with postoperative continuation of MV after initial burn surgery. Maximum intraoperative VIS may provide additional information regarding the hemodynamic component of perioperative severity by quantifying the intensity of vasoactive and inotropic support required during surgery.

papers.abstract: Previous studies showed that administration of inhaled 2-MAC sevoflurane induces gasping in mice by activating a persistent sodium current in the brainstem, an effect blocked by riluzole. However, whether other commonly used volatile anesthetics elicit a similar gasping response in mice has not previously been investigated. This study compared respiratory responses to high doses of three volatile anesthetics. Seven spontaneously breathing adult mice each inhaled one of three anesthetics (sevoflurane, isoflurane, and desflurane) on separate days, and eventually inhaled all three anesthetics. Each anesthetic concentration was increased from 1 MAC to inhaled 2-MAC, while breathing patterns and suprahyoid muscle electromyographic activity (EMGSH) were measured. The effects of riluzole (18 mg/kg, i.p.) on gasping were also tested in five additional mice anesthetized with desflurane and/or isoflurane. All three inhaled anesthetics altered the respiratory pattern from eupnea in 1 MAC to gasping in inhaled 2-MAC in seven mice. However, the time course of ventilation and EMGSH responses to volatile anesthetics at inhaled 2-MAC differed significantly among the three agents: desflurane had the strongest inhibitory effect on inspiratory and EMGSH activities, isoflurane had the weakest inhibitory effects and promoted stable gasping, and sevoflurane showed an intermediate effect. In addition, riluzole administration eliminated isoflurane- and desflurane-induced gasping in five mice. All three anesthetics produced a similar gasping response at inhaled 2-MAC; however, the response's time course and the mechanism by which stable gasping was maintained depend heavily on the volatile anesthetic used.

papers.abstract: To evaluate differences in breast cancer-specific survival (BCSS) overall and across molecular subtypes defined by hormone receptor and HER2 status, and by racial/ethnic groups. The population-based analysis included 99,919 breast cancer cases diagnosed during 2011-2017 in the Florida Cancer Data System. BCSS was estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods and multivariable Cox regression, adjusting for demographic, clinical, socioeconomic, and behavioral factors such as smoking status and disaggregated Asian/Pacific Islander (API) data. Black women had the highest prevalence of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) (22.7%). Compared with White women, mortality risk was higher for Black (HR = 1.36; 95% CI: 1.28-1.44), API (HR = 1.20; 95% CI: 1.04-1.39), and Hispanic women (HR = 1.10; 95% CI: 1.03-1.17). Elevated risks were observed for current smokers, unmarried women, and patients with TNBC (HR = 3.13; 95% CI: 2.96-3.30) compared with HR+/HER2- cases. Disparities were greatest in HR+/HER2- disease, where API and Black women faced 34-46% higher mortality. In TNBC, excess risk persisted for Black women. Once disaggregated, API women no longer had increased risk for breast cancer mortality compared to White women. Receptor-level data revealed disparities for Hispanic and API women, who previously showed survival comparable or better than White women. Florida's size and diversity make these results uniquely informative and may provide insight in BCSS in a heterogenous population. Most concerning is that these disparities are greatest in subtypes with better prognosis and effective therapies. This underscores the need for equitable access to therapies and mitigation of systemic barriers.

papers.abstract: Multicentric IDH-mutant lower-grade gliomas (McLGGs) are rare, and relationships between spatially distinct lesions and long-term oncofunctional management remain poorly characterized. We examined inter-lesional molecular profiles, progression trajectories, and outcomes in patients managed with awake functional-based resection (AFBR). We retrospectively analyzed 9 patients with 18 IDH-mutated glioma sites treated with multimodal therapy including AFBR. Molecular profiles were classified as concordant or discordant based on IDH mutation and 1p/19q-codeletion status, and progression synchrony as synchronous or asynchronous based on imaging, growth kinetics, progression timing, and anaplastic transformation. Surgical sequencing, treatment response, and functional outcomes were assessed longitudinally. Nine patients underwent 17 AFBR during a median 7.8-year follow-up. Defining molecular markers were concordant in 5 patients, discordant in 3, and unresolved in 1, while progression trajectories were asynchronous in 6 and synchronous in 3. Multisite and staged resections were tailored to anatomical and functional considerations. An extent of resection ≥ 90% was achieved in 18 of 22 site-level resections (81.8%), with a median extent of resection of 100%. Six patients received temozolomide, with discordant inter-lesional responses in 3. Among the 8 survivors, median KPS at last follow-up was 90 (range: 80-100). Eight patients maintained or resumed professional or academic activity during at least part of their follow-up, while the remaining patient preserved autonomy and social activities. Neuropsychological findings were descriptive and heterogeneous. McLGGs displayed heterogenous inter-lesional molecular and progression profiles, with molecular concordance not necessarily translating into parallel growth, histopathological evolution, or treatment response. These findings support a longitudinal approach integrating relative inter-lesional behavior with the evolving oncofunctional context. In this selected series, repeated or multisite AFBR was feasible within individualized multimodal treatment trajectories, with generally preserved long-term functional status. N/A.

papers.abstract: For patients with acral melanoma and inguinal nodal metastasis, the optimal extent of groin dissection remains controversial. Whether extending inguinal lymph node dissection (ILND) to ilioinguinal lymph node dissection (IILND) improves survival or alters recurrence patterns in patients without definite pelvic nodal involvement is unclear. Data from all patients with acral melanoma and imaging-suggested isolated inguinal nodal positivity who underwent therapeutic lymph node dissection at Fujian Cancer Hospital (October 2011 to May 2025) were retrieved retrospectively. Overall survival (OS) and relapse-free survival (RFS) were compared using Kaplan-Meier analysis, Cox regression, and overlap weighting. Recurrence patterns were assessed descriptively and by competing-risk analysis. Among 52 eligible patients, 31 underwent ILND and 21 underwent IILND. Median follow-up was 38.6 months. Unadjusted analyses showed no statistically significant differences between IILND and ILND in OS (hazard ratio (HR), 1.16; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.41-3.24; P = 0.783) or RFS (HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.42-1.61; P = 0.569). Secondary overlap-weighted estimates were directionally consistent. Any recurrence occurred in 27/31 patients (87.1%) after ILND and 13/21 patients (61.9%) after IILND. Pelvic nodal recurrence was 29.0% versus 4.8%, respectively, while initial distant metastasis was comparable. Competing-risk analyses showed no significant difference for these recurrence endpoints. IILND did not improve OS or RFS compared with ILND. Crude recurrence patterns suggested fewer pelvic nodal failures after IILND, but this signal was not confirmed in competing-risk analyses or accompanied by survival benefit, supporting selective rather than routine pelvic extension.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the incremental value of adding perirenal fat radiomics to intratumoral computed tomography (CT) radiomics for predicting postoperative progression-free survival (PFS) in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) and to develop a combined radiomics-clinical nomogram for preoperative risk stratification. The study retrospectively enrolled 207 patients with pathologically confirmed RCC who underwent surgery at a single center and randomly divided them into training and validation cohorts at a ratio of 7:3. Radiomics features were extracted from intratumoral and perirenal fat regions on preoperative corticomedullary-phase contrast-enhanced CT images. After feature selection using correlation analysis, univariable Cox regression, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) Cox regression, an intratumoral radiomics model and an intratumoral-perirenal fat radiomics model were constructed. Clinical predictors were identified by uni- and multivariable Cox regression. A combined radiomics-clinical nomogram then was developed. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Kaplan-Meier analysis, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Maximum tumor diameter and fibrinogen were independent clinical predictors of PFS. The intratumoral-perirenal fat model showed better predictive performance than the intratumoral model alone. In the validation cohort, the combined nomogram had AUCs of 0.728, 0.821, and 0.858 for 1-, 2-, and 3-year PFS, respectively, and a concordance index (C-index) of 0.815, outperforming the clinical and radiomics-only models. The nomogram also showed good calibration and clinical utility. Perirenal fat radiomics adds prognostic value beyond intratumoral CT radiomics and, when integrated with clinical factors, enables accurate and noninvasive prediction of postoperative PFS in RCC.

papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine tumors frequently metastasize to the liver. The size and number of neuroendocrine liver metastases (NELM) are prognostic. Studies have often dichotomized these variables, limiting nuanced risk assessment. We aimed to determine whether continuous-variable prognostic models stratified by primary tumor site refine survival prediction after hepatic cytoreduction. We analyzed 329 patients who underwent hepatic cytoreduction for NELM at three international centers during 1995-2024. NELM characteristics, including largest diameter and number of metastases, were modeled as continuous variables. Overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Prognostic contour plots of 10-year OS estimates as a function of largest NELM diameter, plotted on the x-axis, and NELM number, plotted on the y-axis, were generated separately for small intestinal neuroendocrine tumors (SINET) and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PNET). Median follow-up was 11.0 years (95% confidence interval 10.4-15.6). The 10-year OS rate was 71.0% for SINET and 44.4% for PNET (p < 0.001). The 10-year RFS rate was 18.2% for SINET and 4.9% for PNET (p < 0.001). The SINET contour plot had vertical contour lines, indicating that largest tumor diameter was the predominant prognostic factor, whereas the PNET contour plot had diagonal contour lines, indicating that both diameter and number contributed substantially. The prognostic impacts of NELM largest diameter and number differ by tumor origin, with largest diameter predominating in SINET and both diameter and number being important in PNET. Clinicians should not exclude patients from SINET resection solely because of high tumor number.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to compare intraoperative metrics and short-term outcomes between robot-assisted radical proximal gastrectomy (RAPG) and laparoscopic radical proximal gastrectomy (LAPG) for proximal gastric cancer. We retrospectively identified 542 consecutive patients who underwent robot-assisted or laparoscopic radical proximal gastrectomy between December 2018 and December 2024. After exclusions and 1:1 propensity score matching, the final matched cohort included 286 patients, with 143 in each group. Complete surgical videos were reviewed to quantify predefined intraoperative technical events using a modified observational clinical human reliability analysis framework. The primary outcome was Clavien-Dindo grade II or higher complications within 30 days after surgery. Matched statistical methods were used for the propensity score-matched cohort. Compared with LAPG, RAPG was associated with fewer predefined intraoperative technical events, shorter operative time and postoperative length of stay, lower estimated intraoperative blood loss, a greater number of retrieved lymph nodes, and higher inpatient medical costs. Clavien-Dindo grade II or higher complications occurred less frequently after RAPG than after LAPG (14.7% vs. 25.9%; matched odds ratio 0.52; 95% confidence interval 0.29-0.93; exact McNemar P = 0.033). Reflux-related symptoms and eating restriction at 3 months did not differ significantly between groups. In this propensity score-matched cohort study, RAPG was associated with fewer predefined intraoperative technical events and favorable differences in selected short-term perioperative outcomes compared with LAPG, although inpatient medical costs were higher. Early postoperative symptom outcomes were not worse after RAPG.

papers.abstract: Surgery for locally advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (LA-PDAC) remains technically demanding, particularly in presence of extensive venous involvement. A temporary mesenterico-portal shunt (TMPS) facilitates long venous resection and enables safe arterial resection, but evidence is limited to small series. We report technique and outcomes from the largest cohort of TMPS, an approach described at our center. All pancreatic resections performed with TMPS between January 2007 and December 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Operative and survival outcomes were analyzed. 155 LA-PDAC patients underwent TMPS placement. Most had LA-PDAC (92%) and received preoperative chemotherapy (89%), mainly FOLFIRINOX-based (86.9%). Complete venous obstruction (Nakao D) was present in 48.1%. Procedures included pancreatoduodenectomy (62%), total (24.5%), and distal pancreatectomy (13.5%). All patients underwent venous resection; 75% also required arterial resection, most commonly of the superior mesenteric artery (61%). Mean operative time was 610 min (range 180-1145 min). Postoperative mortality was 6.4%, and R0 resection was achieved in 56%. The median OS from diagnosis was 32.7 months (95% confidence interval [CI] 23.5-42.00 months).The median OS from surgery was 17.46 months (95% CI 13.2-21.6 months), with 1-, 3, and 5-year survival rates of 70%, 29%, and 21%, respectively. TMPS is a standardized and reproducible technique that facilitates management of complex venous resection and may enhance the feasibility of arterial resection in selected patients with LA-PDAC.

papers.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) often recurs after resection and has a poor prognosis. Here, we examined the clinicopathological, prognostic, and immune significance of claudin-18 (CLDN18) expression in resected ICC and its relationship with histological duct type. We retrospectively analyzed 120 patients who underwent hepatic resection for ICC and defined CLDN18 positivity as moderate-to-strong membranous staining in at least 75% of tumor cells. We evaluated associations between pathological features, postoperative outcomes, tumor immune microenvironment and public gene expression data. CLDN18 positivity was observed in 25 (20.8%) patients. CLDN18-positive tumors were more frequently located in the perihilar region and more often classified as large duct type, with periductal infiltration, biliary intraepithelial neoplasia, mucin production, perineural invasion, and lymphatic invasion also being more frequent. Patients with CLDN18-positive tumors had poorer overall and recurrence-free survival, and CLDN18 positivity was independently associated with overall (hazard ratio [HR], 2.21; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.20-4.08; P = 0.011) and recurrence-free (HR, 2.00; 95% CI, 1.12-3.55; P = 0.018) survival after adjustment for histological duct type, resection margin status, tumor size, and year of surgery. None of the immune markers differed significantly between the groups after correction for multiple testing. Public database showed higher CLDN18 expression in ICC than that in normal tissues and a significant difference according to American Joint Committee on Cancer stage. CLDN18-positive ICC was frequently associated with the large duct type and its characteristic pathological features, and CLDN18 expression was associated with poor postoperative outcomes after adjustment for histological duct type.

papers.abstract: Population-based evidence on high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) and cervical screening outcomes in Uzbekistan is limited. We assessed hrHPV prevalence, district variation, associated factors, and cytological findings in Tashkent. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 52,995 women aged 18-70 years attending routine cervical screening across Tashkent city during 2024-2025. HR-HPV testing was performed using real-time PCR; reflex liquid-based cytology was performed for all HPV-positive women. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent determinants of HPV positivity (n = 52,995) and cytological abnormality (n = 2,255 HPV-positive women with adequate cytology). Overall HR-HPV positivity was 4.43% (95% CI: 4.26-4.61%), with significant heterogeneity across districts (p < 0.01); Bektemir district recorded the highest prevalence. Independent predictors of HPV positivity included older age (aOR 2.41, 95% CI 1.24-4.83, for 56-70 years), irregular menstruation (aOR 1.39, 95% CI 1.23-1.57), and early sexual debut, while barrier contraception (aOR 0.70, 95% CI 0.60-0.81) and grand multiparity (aOR 0.80, 95% CI 0.65-0.98) were protective. Among HPV-positive women, any cytological abnormality was detected in 24.6% and high-grade lesions in 17.3%. Keratosis was the strongest predictor of cytological abnormality (aOR 4.09-5.16, both p < 0.01). This large population-based study establishes a comprehensive HPV epidemiological baseline for Tashkent and demonstrates the clinical yield of HPV-primary screening with reflexive cytology triage. District-level heterogeneity and identified risk profiles provide evidence for geographically targeted program optimization in support of Uzbekistan's progress toward WHO 90-70-90 cervical cancer elimination targets.

papers.abstract: The use of histone deacetylase inhibitors (HDACis) to reverse epigenetic silencing of immune-associated genes has shown clinical efficacy in hematologic malignancies but not solid tumors. Here we explored the transcriptional and phenotypic effects of in vitro exposures of Zabadinostat, a second-generation class I HDACi, on human peripheral blood mononuclear cells and solid tumor cells to support its combination with immunotherapy. Zabadinostat induced activation of CD8+ and CD4+ T cells and natural killer cells, while reducing the frequency and suppressive function of regulatory T cells. Increases in stem-like memory T cells, a rare subset of multipotent, self-renewing cells important for anti-tumor control, were also observed, and these immune effects coincided with increased expression of transcriptional activation marks H3K9ac and H3K27ac. Zabadinostat increased PD-L1, FAS, ICAM-1, and HLA expression in tumor cells and reverted epithelial-mesenchymal transition-related proteins. These data show that Zabadinostat is a novel immunomodulatory agent with multifaceted effects, capable of enhancing immune effector function, reducing immunosuppression, and improving the visibility of tumor cells to immune-mediated attack. These findings support the use of Zabadinostat in combination with immunotherapeutic agents.

papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have shown great potential for disease detection from liquid biopsies. However, the lack of optimized isolation and detection methods limited their clinical application. Here we engineer a bioinspired, reconfigurable, self-powered bubble motor (Butor) microswarm to streamline intelligent isolation and ultrasensitive profiling of circulating EVs for cancer liquid biopsies. Butor microswarm shows jellyfish-like, self-propelled lifting locomotion along lumen-like vertical or inclined tubular path in parallel, allowing rapid isolation (10 min, near 90%) of EV subtypes via three-dimensional directional scanning capture even in high-viscosity biofluids. Furthermore, the buoyancy-activated Butors achieve ultrasensitive EV profiling near a single-particle level, enable early diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer with an accuracy of up to 94% (95% sensitivity) in a pilot cohort and improve the outcome in cancer staging (I-IV) discrimination, response monitoring of surgical treatment and efficacy prediction of immunotherapy in patients with non-small cell lung cancer. Our self-powered motor represents an intelligent, fast, inexpensive, sensitive and multiplexed liquid biopsy tool for accurate cancer diagnostics and treatment monitoring in clinical settings.

papers.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors have been applied for precise genome engineering in human T cells but poor tropism restricts their efficiency and translational potential. Here, through directed evolution of the AAV6 capsid in primary human T cells, we identified a family of variants containing an APR motif at residues 455-457. The lead candidate, AAV.APR31, enabled robust transduction of primary T and NK cells at nearly 100-1,000-fold lower doses than AAV6 and outperformed the human T cell-tropic capsid AAV-hT7. CRISPR screening identified CD7 as a lineage-specific entry enhancer alongside the canonical AAVR pathway and structural analysis suggested that the APR motif facilitates CD7 engagement. Unlike existing delivery systems confined to one engineering mode, AAV.APR31 enabled transient transgene delivery, site-specific knock-in and transposon integration in human T and NK cells, generating CAR-T cells functionally equivalent to lentiviral vector-manufactured products. Systemic administration of AAV.APR31-generated CAR-T cells in vivo resulted in potent tumor control in hematologic and solid tumor mouse models.

papers.abstract: The optimal discharge strategy after mastectomy, with or without reconstruction, remains debated. Same-day discharge has emerged as a potential paradigm shift in postoperative care, driven by Enhanced Recovery After Surgery protocols and value-based, patient-centered care. This study systematically reviews same-day discharge versus inpatient admission after mastectomy and compares outcomes in a meta-analysis. MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and CINAHL were searched for studies comparing same-day discharge versus inpatient admission after mastectomy, with or without reconstruction. Primary outcomes were 30-day readmission and reoperation. Secondary outcomes included postoperative bleeding, wound infection, unplanned ED or clinic visits, and 30-day mortality. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale and evidence certainty via GRADE. The protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD42024520256). Of 6,377 studies, 18 non-randomized cohort studies encompassing 182,743 patients were included. Same-day discharge was associated with lower odds of reoperation (OR 0.49; 95% CI, 0.41-0.58), postoperative bleeding (OR 0.30; 95% CI, 0.14-0.64), wound infection (OR 0.65; 95% CI, 0.49-0.87), and 30-day mortality (OR 0.07; 95% CI, 0.03-0.19). No significant differences were observed in 30-day readmission (OR 0.96; 95% CI, 0.51-1.81) or unplanned ED or clinic visits (OR 0.62; 95% CI, 0.33-1.16). Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate. This meta-analysis supports the feasibility of same-day discharge after mastectomy, but underscores the need for high-quality randomized trials to validate these findings.

papers.abstract: Esophageal cancer is a highly lethal malignant tumor of the digestive system. Patients with early esophageal cancer often undergo endoscopic resection, but postoperative non-curative resection is frequently undertaken because of the presence of high-risk pathological features. Controversy over subsequent management strategies remains. A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane databases through September 29, 2026, yielded seven studies involving 493 patients. A meta-analysis was performed using random-effects or fixed-effects models, and study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and the Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions-I tool. This meta-analysis included seven studies. Compared with surveillance, additional surgery was associated with significantly improved 5-year survival: 5-year overall survival (risk ratio 1.40; 95% confidence [CI] 1.24-1.58), and 5-year recurrence-free survival (risk ratio 1.34; 95% CI 1.08-1.67), all favoring surgery. The pooled hazard ratio for cancer-specific survival also favored surgery (4.64; 95% CI 1.09-19.76). By contrast, the 3-year endpoints and the time-to-event hazard ratios for overall and recurrence-free survival did not reach statistical significance. Additional surgery offers significant long-term survival benefits for eligible patients with early-stage esophageal cancer. Clinical decision-making should be individualized, and future high-quality studies are needed to further validate its efficacy across diverse populations.

papers.abstract: The ability of cells to adapt their behavior in response to genetic or environmental changes is a fundamental biological process that drives cellular diversity in both normal and pathological contexts, including in tumor evolution. Copy number alterations (CNAs), which can include large-scale changes in genomic ploidy, play a key role in creating adaptive advantages in evolving cell populations. However, tracing these populations across experiments and disentangling the role of CNAs from other sources of transcriptional variability remains challenging and expensive. Here we present Echidna, a Bayesian hierarchical model that integrates single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk whole-genome sequencing data to enable robust integrative inference of CNAs, jointly across samples and treatment time points, to better understand the impact of genomic events on cellular phenotype. Applying Echidna to patient tumor specimens, we demonstrate its superior performance in clonal reconstruction and derive insights into therapy resistance mechanisms.

papers.abstract: To describe acute diencephalic syndrome (ADS) after superior transventricular surgery for giant pituitary adenomas with true third-ventricular extension, and to explore the association of ADS with extent of resection in a selected cohort. We retrospectively analyzed 40 adults operated on in 2015-2025 (23 total, 17 subtotal resections; 22 anterior transcallosal and 18 transcortical transventricular approaches). Postoperative AVP-D was distinguished from multidomain ADS, graded retrospectively according to the previously published four-stage framework. Final-stage agreement was reassessed independently in all 40 patients. Postoperative AVP-D occurred in all 40 patients; four had isolated AVP-D without ADS. ADS occurred in 36/40 (90.0%): 23/23 after total and 13/17 after subtotal resection (risk difference 23.5 percentage points; 95% Newcombe CI 3.5-47.3; two-sided Fisher exact p = 0.026). Stage III-IV ADS occurred in 9/23 versus 3/17 (p = 0.179). Independent final-stage agreement was 36/40 (90.0%; linear-weighted κ = 0.926). Five patients required mechanical ventilation, and two died. ADS was frequent in this anatomically selected transventricular cohort, but the operational definition is not specific for hypothalamic injury and the observational comparison is vulnerable to confounding by indication. The observed lower ADS frequency after subtotal resection is hypothesis-generating. Prospective multicenter validation is necessary.

papers.abstract: Second ipsilateral breast cancers present unique treatment challenges for patients that have formerly received breast-conserving surgery (BCS) with radiation therapy (RT). We utilized the population-based Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database to characterize temporal and regional trends in treatment selection for second breast cancer across the US. We identified a sample of 20,258 women diagnosed with second primary cancers between 2005 and 2022 who had previously received BCS with RT. Multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression models were fitted to determine associations between demographic, clinical, and geographic factors and the likelihood of receiving BCS with RT. In ipsilateral cancers, use of BCS with RT relative to mastectomy was significantly more likely from 2020 to 2022 compared to from 2005 to 2009 (odds ratio [OR] 5.16, 95% CI 2.99-8.90). BCS with RT was less likely in women with larger tumor size and hormone-receptor (HR) negative disease (OR 0.27 for tumors > 5.0 cm vs. tumors < 0.5 cm, 0.58 for HR- vs. HR+) Regional variation in treatment selection was significant for ipsilateral cancers, with an observed intraclass correlation coefficient within regions of 0.14 for relative usage of BCS with RT vs. mastectomy. Our findings quantify the extent of regional variation in treatment selection and describe key trends and characteristics of the patient population receiving radiation for second primary breast cancers.

papers.abstract: The aims of this project were to devise and benchmark internationally applicable quality indicators (QIs) for palliative radiotherapy (RT) "near end of life". To the best of our knowledge, this is the first multinational attempt at consensus on QIs for any palliative RT setting. Radiation and clinical oncologists with expertise in palliative RT, and cancer consumer advocates were invited to undertake a Delphi survey. The 30/30 invited panelists comprised 27 clinicians from nine countries and three consumers from XXXX and New Zealand, denoting a replicability in the upper range of "moderate" (defined as 60% to <80%). The panel initially agreed upon a definition of near end of life for patients undergoing palliative radiotherapy ("A state of irreversible functional decline from cancer and a short prognosis often measured in weeks or months"), and a timepoint criterion for benchmarking the subsequent QIs ("Patients dying within 30-days of starting palliative RT"). Nine candidate QIs were curated by the XXXX prior to the voluntary, anonymous survey which utilized an online platform (SurveyMonkey). Responses were appraised by an XXXX steering sub-committee, with 75% agreement defined as the iterative consensus threshold. The response rate for each of four Delphi rounds was 30/30 (100%). Supported QIs for near end of life patients relating to life expectancy documentation (2), waiting time for RT (1) and RT fractionation (2) were each benchmarked at ≥80%, with ≤30% for 30-day mortality. Additionally, the panel benchmarked conventional 30-day mortality (for all palliative RT patients) at ≤20%. Seven QIs were accepted and benchmarked, six for palliative RT near end of life, and one for all palliative RT patients. Real-world testing of the feasibility of these QIs and achievability of the benchmarks is required.

papers.abstract: This phase I/II single-arm trial assessed the tolerability and efficacy of stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) to all tumours plus intermittent androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) in patients with oligometastatic hormone sensitive prostate cancer (HSPC). Primary endpoint was the incidence of grade 3+ SBRT induced adverse events (AE's), including radiotherapy induced bone fractures. Secondary endpoints included failure-free survival (FFS), cumulative incidence of developing castration resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), and overall survival (OS). Eligible patients had synchronous or metachronous oligometastases (≤ 5 metastases, with ≤ 3 metastases in any one organ system) identified on conventional imaging. SBRT was delivered to all lesions, along with 1 year of ADT before stopping. Intermittent ADT (using 1 year cycles) was restarted when the prostate specific antigen (PSA) reached > 10 ng/mL, if new metastases developed, or earlier at the discretion of the physician. SBRT could be delivered to any new oligometastases that developed while off ADT in conjunction with restarting ADT. Eighty-nine evaluable patients with 171 metastases were enrolled. Median follow-up was 74.7 months. Thirty-three patients (37.1%) had synchronous disease presentation. Six patients (6.7%) experienced grade 3 AE's (5 patients with vertebral fractures and 1 patient with urinary tract obstruction). The 5-year cumulative incidence of restarting ADT and developing CRPC were 59.7% and 22.8% respectively. Five-year FFS and OS were 15.2% and 78.2% respectively. Higher PSA nadir after SBRT and 1 year of ADT was significantly associated with developing subsequent CRPC and worse OS. At time of last follow-up, 35 patients (39.3%) were alive with HSPC and not on ADT. SBRT and intermittent ADT for oligometastatic HSPC was safe and resulted in favourable long-term outcomes. A small proportion of patients did not progress in any way after SBRT and 1 year of ADT.

papers.abstract: Etentamig is an investigational B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) x CD3 bispecific T-cell engager, composed of a low-affinity CD3 binding domain, potentially reducing cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and infections, a high-avidity bivalent BCMA-binding domain, and retained FcRn binding supporting monthly (Q4W) dosing after a single step-up dose (SUD). We report long-term efficacy and safety from the ongoing, open-label, phase 1 (dose escalation/expansion; NCT03933735) and Arm A of the phase 1b (NCT05650632) studies of etentamig in adult patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, triple-class exposure, and ≥3 prior lines of therapy (LoT). In phase 1, patients received etentamig 60 mg Q4W or 40 mg Q3W, and in phase 1b, a SUD on Day 1 and 60 mg Q4W on Day 4. Among 146 patients (median age: 68 years; median [range] prior LoT: 4 [3-23]), median follow-up was 13 months (range: 1-48). Objective responses and ≥ very good partial responses occurred in 66% and 54% of patients. Median duration of response and progression-free survival were not reached. Pooled data suggest etentamig has a manageable safety profile, with Grade 3/4 neutropenia and infection occurring in 38% and 23% of patients. In phase 1b Arm A (n=23), overall CRS incidence was 30% (26% Grade 1; 4% Grade 2) with modified dexamethasone premedication and 1 SUD; median onset was 22.3 hours (range: 5.5-29.6) hours, with resolution in 20.7 hours (range: 1.8-131.7). Etentamig's molecular design may be associated with the observed clinical efficacy and tolerability while also potentially supporting extended dosing intervals.

papers.abstract: The prognostic significance of biopsy-to-radical prostatectomy (RP) ISUP grade discordance relative to final RP pathology remains unclear. We evaluated its association with prostate cancer-specific mortality (PCSM) and overall survival (OS). Using the SEER database (n = 30,303), propensity score matching yielded balanced cohorts for upgrading (n = 7,254 pairs) and downgrading (n = 3,671 pairs). Fine-Gray competing-risk regression assessed PCSM, and Cox regression assessed OS. Sensitivity analyses replaced biopsy ISUP grade with final RP ISUP grade in multivariable Fine-Gray models, and multicollinearity was evaluated by using adjusted generalized variance inflation factors. In biopsy ISUP-adjusted matched analyses, upgrading was associated with a higher risk of PCSM (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 2.15; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.49-3.11; P < 0.001), whereas downgrading was associated with a lower risk of PCSM (sHR 0.40; 95% CI 0.27-0.60; P < 0.001). Downgrading was also associated with improved OS in the original matched analysis (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.66-0.96; P = 0.017), whereas upgrading was not significantly associated with OS. However, after replacing biopsy ISUP grade with final RP ISUP grade in sensitivity analyses, neither upgrading (sHR 0.73; 95% CI 0.45-1.19; P = 0.21) nor downgrading (sHR 1.46; 95% CI 0.87-2.46; P = 0.16) remained significantly associated with PCSM. Collinearity diagnostics showed no substantial multicollinearity. Biopsy-to-RP ISUP discordance was associated with PCSM in biopsy grade-adjusted analyses, but these associations were attenuated after adjustment for final RP ISUP grade. Final surgical pathology remains the dominant prognostic factor, and discordance should be interpreted as a prognostic/predictive signal rather than an independent biological driver.

papers.abstract: The prognostic significance of enlarged lateral pelvic lymph nodes (LPLNs) in patients with rectal cancer undergoing nonoperative management (NOM) remains unclear. This study evaluated whether pretreatment LPLN enlargement is associated with local regrowth or distant metastasis after NOM. The study retrospectively analyzed 77 patients with low rectal cancer who underwent NOM after radiotherapy-based neoadjuvant treatment between 2014 and 2025. Pretreatment LPLN enlargement was defined as a short-axis diameter of ≥ 7 mm on baseline magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Local regrowth-free survival (LRFS) and distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) were evaluated according to pretreatment LPLN enlargement. Pretreatment LPLN enlargement was present in 17 patients (22.1%). Among these patients, the median LPLN short-axis diameter decreased from 8 to 3 mm after treatment. During a median follow-up period of 55 months, local regrowth occurred in 15 patients (19.5%) and distant metastasis in 9 patients (11.7%). Pretreatment LPLN enlargement was not significantly associated with LRFS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.39; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.38-4.05; P = 0.587) but was associated with poorer DMFS (HR, 4.70; 95% CI, 1.24-19.01; P = 0.024). In an exploratory analysis treating local regrowth as a time-dependent covariate, pretreatment LPLN enlargement remained associated with distant metastasis (HR, 4.49; 95% CI, 1.20-16.84; P = 0.026). Pretreatment LPLN enlargement was associated with distant metastasis but not significantly associated with local regrowth in patients undergoing NOM despite substantial nodal regression after neoadjuvant treatment. Pretreatment LPLN enlargement may retain prognostic significance as a marker of metastatic potential in patients selected for NOM.

papers.abstract: Germline single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) are biomarkers that can be readily measured using DNA from peripheral blood or normal tissue. While SNPs have been associated with survival and cytotoxic chemotherapy response in several cancers, limited data exist on the clinical relevance of selected SNPs in oesophageal cancer (OeC) patients. DNA was extracted from normal tissue of 480 OeC patients treated with either surgery alone (S, n = 233) or chemotherapy followed by surgery (CS, n = 247) in the OE02 trial. SNPs in DPYD, OPRT, ERCC1, ERCC2 and XRCC1, GSTP1 and TS were analysed using MassARRAY, Sanger sequencing or gel electrophoresis. Associations with clinicopathological variables and overall survival (OS) were investigated. Selected SNP variants were associated with age, tumour differentiation, tumour regression and OS. The OPRT rs1801019 'GC' genotype was more frequent in patients aged >65 years (p = 0.034); the TS 5'UTR '3R/3R' genotype was more frequent in poorly differentiated tumours (p = 0.019) and the ERCC2 rs13181 'GG' genotype was nominally associated with improved tumour regression (p = 0.041). In an exploratory analysis, the ERCC1 rs11615 'CT' genotype was associated with improved OS (HR 0.80, 95%CI: 0.65-0.99, p = 0.040) in the whole cohort and in the subgroup of patients with adenocarcinoma treated by surgery alone. No associations were observed for any of the other SNPs. In the largest germline SNP analysis in OeC to date, ERCC1 rs11615 'CT' emerged as a candidate prognostic biomarker warranting validation in an independent cohort.

papers.abstract: CD8 T cells can make a decisive contribution to anticancer immune responses. While the glycoprotein CD101 is present on effector CD8 T cells, the signaling pathways driving CD101 expression and the outcome of CD101 engagement on CD8 T cells are elusive. Here, we show that the activation of TGF-β signaling induces CD101 on mouse and human CD8 T cells. CD101 expression on CD8 T cells was dependent on TCR signaling and TGF-β-induced Smad3. In multiple cancers, we found that mouse and human CD8(+) CD101(+) tumor infiltrating lymphocytes exhibited a resident memory phenotype, as illustrated by co-expression of CD69 and CD103. Accordingly, CD101-deficient mice featured accelerated tumor growth and were unable to respond to anti-PD-1 therapy. Altogether, these results suggest that CD101 expression on CD8 T cells has functional relevance and can be therapeutically exploited for anticancer therapy.

papers.abstract: Relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) has a poor prognosis, highlighting the need for more targeted and less toxic therapeutic options. CD371, enriched on leukemic stem and chemoresistant AML cells but less prevalent on hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), is an attractive chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy target. We describe the optimization and preclinical validation of a fully human CD371-directed CD28/CD3ζ CAR T-cell product that constitutively secretes interleukin (IL)-18. CAR T-cells with single-chain variable fragments (scFvs) in the VH-VL orientation outperformed VL-VH constructs both in vitro and in vivo. While constructs with three to five linkers (H3-5L) performed similarly in vivo, those with five linkers (H5L) demonstrated improved in vivo survival. IL-18 secretion further augmented efficacy against both antigen-high and antigen-low/negative tumors. Notably, IL-18-armored CAR T-cells exhibited superior activity against antigen-low/negative tumors, in part due to “bystander killing” mediated by increased interferon-γ production and FAS-L upregulation. In vitro colony-forming unit assays using CD34+umbilical cord blood HSCs demonstrated reduced toxicity compared with non-optimized constructs. Based on these preclinical findings, this CD371-directed scFv is currently being evaluated in two first-in-human phase 1 clinical trials for relapsed or refractory AML (NCT06017258 and NCT06128044).

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors show limited efficacy in previously treated recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer (rmCC). BVAC-C is an autologous B cell-based and monocyte-based therapeutic vaccine targeting human papillomavirus (HPV)16/18 E6 and E7 oncoproteins. We report a phase II trial—representing the first clinical evaluation of a B cell– and monocyte-based therapeutic HPV vaccine combined with a programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitor—evaluating BVAC-C combined with durvalumab in patients with HPV16/18-positive rmCC who had progressed after platinum-based chemotherapy. This single-arm, open-label, two-part phase II trial was registered prospectively at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04800978) on 15 March 2021, before enrollment of the first participant. 30 patients received treatment; 29 were evaluable for efficacy. The objective response rate (ORR) was 37.9% (six complete responses and five partial responses), and the disease control rate was 62.1%. The 6-month progression-free survival (PFS) rate was 51.7% and median PFS was 8.7 months (95% CI 4.0 to 24.3 months). Patients with a treatment-free interval >6 months achieved a significantly higher ORR (52.9% vs 16.7%; p=0.047). Notably, the median duration of response was 20 months and complete responders showed sustained remission beyond 18 months, raising the possibility of functional cure in a subset of patients. Antigen-specific T-cell responses and cytokine activation were robust and PD-L1-independent. BVAC-C plus durvalumab showed encouraging antitumor activity with a manageable safety profile, supporting further evaluation in HPV-positive rmCC. NCT04800978.

papers.abstract: CD8+ T cells differentiate into terminally exhausted T cells, a hypofunctional state induced in tumor environments that leads to impaired antitumor immunity and poor cancer prognosis. Therapeutic approaches to improve effector CD8+ T-cell function by limiting or reversing tumor-mediated exhaustion are areas of active investigation. Terminally exhausted CD8+ T cells from tumors exhibit increased transcriptional repression of effector genes by tri-methylation of histone 3 lysine 27 (H3K27me3). Enhancer of zeste homolog 2 (Ezh2) is a crucial enzyme acting as the catalytic core of the polycomb repressive complex 2, which adds H3K27me3 in T cells. Using pharmacologic and genetic suppression of Ezh2, we evaluated its role in driving CD8+ T-cell exhaustion in vitro and in murine melanoma models in vivo, including its impact on functional restoration. Ezh2 expression is significantly increased in CD8+ T cells exposed to chronic stimulation. Suppression of Ezh2 significantly increased the proportion of CD8+ T cells expressing both tumor necrosis factor and interferon-γ when exposed to chronic stimulation in vitro or in the tumor. Ezh2-deficient CD8+ T cells also exhibited decreases in the exhaustion-mediated transcription factor Tox. Multiple genes were upregulated when Ezh2 was deleted, including cytokines related to type 1 (eg, Gzmc) and type 2 (eg, Il13) immunity, and treatment with interleukin (IL)-4 induced a significantly higher proportion of IL-13-expressing CD8+ T cells. These findings suggest that Ezh2 contributes to epigenetic modifications supporting T-cell exhaustion, and Ezh2 suppression or deletion can rescue effector functions of exhausted CD8+ T cells. Thus, Ezh2 may be a therapeutic target to improve antitumor immunity.

papers.abstract: Survival outcomes for patients with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) are poor when disease is refractory to rituximab, with or without chemotherapy, highlighting a clear need for alternative therapeutic strategies. Adoptive cellular therapy (ACT) has been explored as a means of providing memory T-cell support, but its therapeutic role in refractory EBV infection remains incompletely defined. This retrospective multicenter study included 17 pediatric and adult allo-HCT recipients (age range, 7–66 years) with EBV infections refractory to ≥1 line of anti-EBV therapy who received CD45RA-depleted ACT. Of the 17 patients, 10 (58.82%) had EBV-associated post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder. The first CD45RA-depleted T-cell infusion was administered at a median of 117 days (range, 50–696 days) after allo-HCT, at a cumulative dose of 20×10⁶ cells/kg (range, 8.09–51.13×10⁶ cells/kg), with a median of two infusion cycles (range, 1–6); four patients also received concurrent intrathecal ACT. 15 patients (88.24%) achieved an overall response. The median follow-up was 482 days (range, 44–933 days). The 90-day EBV DNA clearance rate was 82.35% (95% CI 48.18% to 94.97%). Treatment was well tolerated; emergent adverse events included acute graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) in two patients (11.76%), chronic GvHD in seven (41.18%), and primary disease relapse in one (5.88%). The 1-year overall survival rate was 76.47% (95% CI 48.83% to 90.45%). CD45RA-depleted T-cell ACT provides clinical benefit in patients with EBV infection refractory to ≥1 line of anti-EBV therapy after allo-HCT, with a favorable safety profile in this cohort.

papers.abstract: Short preoperative immune induction could inform future breast-cancer trials, but it must not delay surgery. BreastVAX tested whether a single-dose preoperative regimen could be delivered within the planned surgical window while collecting safety and biological data. BreastVAX (NCT04454528) was a single-centre, open-label, phase 1b/2 window-of-opportunity trial. Adults with operable invasive breast cancer scheduled for upfront surgery received one 200 mg pembrolizumab infusion alone or with one 7 Gy tumour-directed radiotherapy fraction before or after pembrolizumab. The primary phase 1b endpoint was feasibility, defined as completion of assigned preoperative treatment within 21 days without delaying surgery by more than 14 days. Phase 2 had two descriptive interim reviews. In phase 1b, all six enrolled participants met the feasibility criterion. Across both phases, all 30 treated participants completed assigned preoperative therapy and underwent surgery without protocol-defined delay; median follow-up was 634 days (IQR 256-1120). Most adverse events were grade 1-2, with no deaths and no treatment-related grade 3 or higher events; the only grade 3 event was a surgical re-excision unrelated to treatment. Pathological and immune-correlative findings were exploratory and showed treatment-associated immune changes, including a neoepitope-reactive T-cell response in one responder. Pembrolizumab, with or without a single subablative tumour-directed radiotherapy fraction, was delivered within the preoperative window without protocol-defined surgical delay. Larger biomarker-informed studies should evaluate sequence prospectively, use endpoints suited to this short regimen, and prespecify harms monitoring. papers.abstract: HR+/HER2- breast cancer is the most prevalent molecular subtype of breast cancer, yet overall pathological complete response (pCR) rates after neoadjuvant chemotherapy remain low. BRCA mutations and homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) may sensitize tumors to PARP inhibitors through synthetic lethality. We investigated the efficacy and safety of fluzoparib combined with neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with HRD-positive and/or germline BRCA (gBRCA)-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer. This single-center, prospective, open-label, single-arm phase II trial (NCT07162051) enrolled women aged 18-70 years with newly diagnosed HRD-positive and/or gBRCA-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer. Patients received fluzoparib combined with docetaxel during cycles 1-4, followed by epirubicin plus cyclophosphamide during cycles 5-8. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving residual cancer burden (RCB) grade 0/I. Secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), pathological complete response (pCR) rate, and safety. Twenty-eight patients were enrolled between March 2023 and October 2025. Four patients (14.3%; 95% CI 4.0%-32.7%) achieved RCB 0/I, two patients (7.1%; 95% CI 0.9%-23.5%) achieved total pCR (tpCR), and six patients (21.4%; 95% CI 8.3%-41.0%) achieved breast pCR (bpCR). The ORR was 82.1%. Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in four patients (14.3%). No treatment discontinuations, dose reductions, treatment delays, or treatment-related deaths were observed. The addition of fluzoparib to standard neoadjuvant chemotherapy did not improve RCB 0/I rates in HRD-positive and/or gBRCA-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer, although the regimen was well tolerated. Future studies should focus on gBRCA-mutated or higher-risk populations and explore optimized combination strategies, including anti-angiogenic agents.
